title: Instrument analytics pipeline: SLIs/SLOs, distributed tracing, and dashboard surfaces
creator: Marina Chen
description: Goal: Improve observability for Console backend analytics services and the usage analytics data pipeline so engineering and SRE can reliably detect regressions in data freshness, completeness, processing errors, and dashboard query latency. Scope: instrument the ingestion path (collector -> Kafka -> transforms -> materializer), the aggregation/query layer backing Console dashboards, and the worker fleet that runs batch/stream transforms. Deliverables: a set of SLIs and SLOs, distributed tracing spans propagated across services, structured logging conventions for analytics events, alert rules, and a Grafana dashboard pack for on-call and product KPI visibility. Non-goals: re-architecting pipeline storage or changing schema definitions (separate initiative).
acceptance_criteria: SLIs defined and documented for ingestion delay (P50/P90/P99), event processing success rate, per-tenant data completeness, and query latency; SLOs agreed with PM/ops
Tracing implemented end-to-end: trace-id injected at collector and visible through Kafka consumers and DB writes for at least 90% of traffic in canary

Structured logs emitted by ingestion and transform services with consistent fields (event_id, tenant_id, pipeline_stage, error_code), and stored in central logging with 7d retention for analytics alerts
Grafana dashboard created with panels for SLO burn rate, pipeline throughput, per-region ingestion delay, error rate by stage, and per-tenant anomalies; dashboards linked from Console runbook
Alerting rules in Alertmanager: sustained error rate >1% for 5m, ingestion delay 95th percentile > 2x SLO, and missing data for a tenant (no events for expected window)
Instrumentation rollout completed behind a feature flag to 10% traffic for 72h, validation performed via load test and smoke queries, followed by ramp to 100%
